about: An invented learner for tests and evals. Not based on any real person.
summary: University statistics final in 3 weeks (2 Nov 2026), needs 70%. Windows laptop, Apple Calendar on an iPhone (no connector, so an .ics file). Two hours a day, every day.
first_message: my stats final is in 3 weeks and I'm behind. can you make me a real plan and test me every day

replies.reply: Pass my intro statistics final with at least 70%. It's required for my major and I got 58% on the midterm.

Monday 2 November, 9 am, two hours. Calculator allowed, and the department gives us a one-page formula sheet. Nothing from this gets handed in for a grade, the homework is finished. The syllabus says no AI on graded work.
58% on the midterm, and I can open the graded midterm with marks per question right now. Most of the homework I did with a study group, so don't trust that.
Lecture slides, the textbook, the homework sets, and three past finals with solutions. Follow the textbook's notation, please.

expected.match_note: Ids, enums, numbers, dates and times are compared exactly. Free-text values (goal, why, success, notes, what) are compared by meaning, not wording. Objects inside lists are compared on the keys given.

Do not calibrate on: homework done with the study group
the midterm total on its own (the item-level marks may be looked at; the diagnostic decides)
Learner notes: Wants practice exams at 9:00, the real exam time
If I feel the urge to cram the night before, then I do the normal session and sleep instead

readback_mentions: Statistics final on Mon 2 Nov 2026, 70% or more
120 min × 7 days, about 14 h a week, ceiling about 19.6 h
calculator and the one-page formula sheet, as in the exam
an .ics file to import into Apple Calendar; later changes come as a short list
nothing handed in for a grade; the course's AI rule is recorded
readback_mentions_if_permission_prompt: the one permission rule, with the Windows launcher: Bash(py -3 *indelible.py*)
checks: No file exists in the workspace before the readback 'yes'.
Scripts are run with the py -3 launcher, and every file is read and written as UTF-8.
The past-paper solutions are registered as keys and stay sealed until the matching attempt is filed.
Past finals are used for measurement, at 9:00 where possible, and never within 3 hours after another measurement.
Each 120-minute session is budgeted with 3 minutes to open, 8 to close, a work fraction of 0.6 and one 10-minute break.
A daily 15-minute retrieval slot is proposed as an if-then plan (sessions of 120 minutes or more).
Nothing is planned in class or job hours, or within 30 minutes of the 00:30 bedtime; 2026-10-27 is kept clear.
Weekly planned minutes stay at or under 1176.
The calendar is delivered as an .ics file; no calendar connector is called.
Claude never writes work the learner will hand in for a grade.
Learner-facing text contains no E-, B-, S- or L- ids, no answers and no emojis.
